nodes.label: Trigonometry
nodes.note: Ratios, allied angles, compound and multiple-angle formulas, triangle identities, equations, and height-distance applications. JEE tests formula recall under algebraic manipulation.

nodes.label: Trigonometric Ratios and Identities
nodes.note: Definitions and the fundamental identities that everything else uses.

nodes.label: Six Ratios
nodes.note: Sine, cosine, tangent and their reciprocals on a right triangle: $$\sin \theta = \frac{opp}{hyp}, \ \cos \theta = \frac{adj}{hyp}, \ \tan \theta = \frac{opp}{adj}$$. The reciprocal pairings $csc = 1/sin$, $sec = 1/cos$, $cot = 1/tan$ complete the set.

nodes.label: Reciprocal Relations
nodes.note: Cosecant, secant, and cotangent are reciprocals: $$\csc \theta = \frac{1}{\sin \theta}, \ \sec \theta = \frac{1}{\cos \theta}, \ \cot \theta = \frac{1}{\tan \theta}$$. JEE options often hide reciprocal traps among near-identical choices.

nodes.label: Pythagorean Identities
nodes.note: $$\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta = 1, \ 1 + \tan^2 \theta = \sec^2 \theta, \ 1 + \cot^2 \theta = \csc^2 \theta$$. Divide the first identity by $\cos^2$ or $\sin^2$ to get the other two.

nodes.label: Standard Exact Values
nodes.note: Key angles: $$\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}, \ \cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}, \ \tan 45^\circ = 1$$. A memory table for $0^\circ, 30^\circ, 45^\circ, 60^\circ, 90^\circ$ is non-negotiable.

nodes.label: Identity Reduction
nodes.note: Simplify compound expressions by rewriting in sine and cosine: e.g. $$\tan \theta + \cot \theta = \frac{\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta \cos \theta} = \frac{2}{\sin 2\theta}$$. JEE 'prove that' items demand this conversion.

nodes.label: Example: Simplification
nodes.note: $\frac{\sin \theta}{1 - \cos \theta} = \cot(\theta/2)$ follows by multiplying numerator and denominator by $1 + \cos \theta$ and using $1 - \cos^2 = \sin^2$.

nodes.label: Allied Angles and ASTC
nodes.note: Signs and reductions for angles in all quadrants.

nodes.label: ASTC Rule
nodes.note: Quadrant signs: all positive in I, sine positive in II, tangent positive in III, cosine positive in IV. 'All Snakes Take Coffee' is the memory hook for which ratios are positive in each quadrant.

nodes.label: Allied Angle Reduction
nodes.note: Reduce any angle to a first-quadrant reference: $$\sin(90^\circ \pm \theta) = \cos \theta, \ \sin(180^\circ \pm \theta) = \mp \sin \theta$$. Sign from ASTC, cofunction swap for odd multiples of 90.

nodes.label: Mini-Example: Reduction
nodes.note: $\cos 150^\circ = \cos(180^\circ - 30^\circ) = -\cos 30^\circ = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. Minutes of error in sign sink most JEE one-markers.

nodes.label: Compound Angles
nodes.note: Sum and difference formulas plus product-to-sum conversions.

nodes.label: Addition and Subtraction
nodes.note: $$\sin(A \pm B) = \sin A \cos B \pm \cos A \sin B$$ $$\cos(A \pm B) = \cos A \cos B \mp \sin A \sin B$$ $$\tan(A \pm B) = \frac{\tan A \pm \tan B}{1 \mp \tan A \tan B}$$. Every compound-angle JEE item starts here.

nodes.label: Sum-to-Product (C and D) Formulas
nodes.note: $$\sin C + \sin D = 2 \sin \frac{C+D}{2} \cos \frac{C-D}{2}$$ and similarly for $\sin C - \sin D$, $\cos C \pm \cos D$. Factoring sums is how trig series telescoped in JEE.

nodes.label: Product-to-Sum Formulas
nodes.note: $$2\sin A \cos B = \sin(A+B) + \sin(A-B)$$ $$2\cos A \cos B = \cos(A+B) + \cos(A-B)$$. Multiplication terms collapse into sums, easing integration-style algebra.

nodes.label: Multiple and Sub-Multiple Angles
nodes.note: Double, triple, and half-angle relations plus special products.

nodes.label: Double Angle Relations
nodes.note: $$\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta, \ \cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta, \ \tan 2\theta = \frac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta}$$. Half-angle forms come from reversing them.

nodes.label: Triple Angle Relations
nodes.note: $$\sin 3\theta = 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta, \ \cos 3\theta = 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta$$. Factor these as cubics in $\sin$ or $\cos$ for equations.

nodes.label: Symmetrical Triplet Product
nodes.note: $$\cos\theta \cos(60^\circ - \theta)\cos(60^\circ + \theta) = \frac{1}{4}\cos 3\theta$$. A frequently regurgitated JEE identity for max-min on trig products.

nodes.label: Half-Angle Substitutions
nodes.note: $$\sin \theta = \frac{2t}{1+t^2}, \ \cos \theta = \frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}, \ t = \tan(\theta/2)$$. The t-substitution rationalizes trig equations.

nodes.label: Conditional Identities in a Triangle
nodes.note: When $A + B + C = \pi$, special relations between the angles appear.

nodes.label: Linear Conditional Identity
nodes.note: If $A + B + C = \pi$: $$\sin A + \sin B + \sin C = 4\cos\frac{A}{2}\cos\frac{B}{2}\cos\frac{C}{2}$$. Sum-to-product on two terms starts the proof.

nodes.label: Tangent Conditional Identity
nodes.note: In a triangle: $$\tan A + \tan B + \tan C = \tan A \tan B \tan C$$. Also $\tan\frac{A}{2}\tan\frac{B}{2} + \tan\frac{B}{2}\tan\frac{C}{2} + \tan\frac{C}{2}\tan\frac{A}{2} = 1$.

nodes.label: Cosine Conditional Identity
nodes.note: In a triangle: $$\cos A + \cos B + \cos C = 1 + 4\sin\frac{A}{2}\sin\frac{B}{2}\sin\frac{C}{2}$$. This converts a cosine sum into a product of half-angle sines.

nodes.label: Trigonometric Equations
nodes.note: General solutions and the linear-equation trick.

nodes.label: Standard General Solutions
nodes.note: $$\sin \theta = \sin \alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi + (-1)^n \alpha$$ $$\cos \theta = \cos \alpha \Rightarrow \theta = 2n\pi \pm \alpha$$ $$\tan \theta = \tan \alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi + \alpha$$. All n are integers.

nodes.label: Linear Equation a cos + b sin = c
nodes.note: Divide by $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ and write as $\cos(\theta - \alpha) = c/\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ where $\tan \alpha = b/a$. Solvability needs $|c| \le \sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.

nodes.label: Cofunction Identities
nodes.note: Complementary angles swap sine and cosine: $$\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \cos \theta, \ \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \cot \theta$$. Used when two angles in a problem sum to $\pi/2$.

nodes.label: Example: General Solution
nodes.note: $\sin 2\theta = \sin \theta$ gives $2\theta = n\pi + (-1)^n \theta$, splitting into $\theta = 2n\pi/3$ or $\theta = \pi + 2n\pi$.

nodes.label: Height and Distance
nodes.note: Angles of elevation and depression with sine and cosine rules.

nodes.label: Angle of Elevation
nodes.note: The angle between the horizontal and the line of sight to an object above. With height h and base distance d: $$\tan \alpha = \frac{h}{d}$$. Theodolite problems always start with a right triangle.

nodes.label: Angle of Depression
nodes.note: The angle between the horizontal and the line of sight to an object below. By alternate interior angles, depression from A to B equals elevation from B to A.

nodes.label: Example: Tower and Shadow
nodes.note: A tower casts a shadow of length 20 m at elevation $60^\circ$: $h = 20 \tan 60^\circ = 20\sqrt{3}$ m.

nodes.label: Sine and Cosine Rules in Triangulation
nodes.note: For oblique triangles: $$\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C} = 2R$$ and $$c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C$$. Use when the pole leans or the two stations are not level.

nodes.label: Max-Min and Series
nodes.note: Boundedness of trig expressions and arithmetic-angle series.

nodes.label: Max of a sin + b cos
nodes.note: $$a\sin\theta + b\cos\theta \in [-\sqrt{a^2+b^2}, \ \sqrt{a^2+b^2}]$$. This single bound answers most 'range of expression' questions.

nodes.label: Quadratic Trig Forms
nodes.note: Rewrite $a\sin^2\theta + b\sin\theta\cos\theta + c\cos^2\theta$ using double-angle identities to separate a constant and a single $\sin 2\theta / \cos 2\theta$ term.

nodes.label: Example: Range via Bound
nodes.note: The range of $f(\theta) = 3\sin\theta + 4\cos\theta$ is $[-5, 5]$ since $\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5$, so no solving of the equation is needed.

nodes.label: Sine and Cosine Series in AP
nodes.note: $$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \sin(a + kd) = \frac{\sin(nd/2)}{\sin(d/2)} \sin\left(a + \frac{(n-1)d}{2}\right)$$. Multiply and divide by $2\sin(d/2)$ to get a telescoping product-to-sum series.
